key_insight: AgentHOI uses a training-free, agentic multimodal workflow to improve open-world human-object interaction detection by combining iterative reasoning with precise localization instead of learning HOI classifiers.
engineering_relevance: This approach is valuable for deploying HOI systems in real-world settings where interaction categories are open-ended, ambiguous, and costly to annotate.
method: Context-aware multi-round reasoning progressively refines HOI hypotheses to improve discovery coverage.
Multifaceted interaction localization generates instance-specific descriptions using semantic, spatial, and appearance cues.
Orchestrates complementary vision foundation modules for coordinated semantic reasoning and spatial grounding without HOID training data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing AgentHOI outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and weakly supervised methods in real-world settings without requiring HOID training data.
watch_item: Because the system relies on modular foundation-model reasoning and prompting, performance may depend on prompt quality, module coordination, and robustness in highly cluttered scenes.
paper_title: Unleashing Multimodal Large Language Models for Training-free HOI Detection in the Wild
